title: WPMS/2631/2012 of DESH RAJ and OTHERS Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND and OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2631 of 2012
Desh Raj S/O Krishna Lal and others
... Petitioners.
Versus
State of Uttarakhand through Collector Haridwar and two others.
... Respondents.
Mr. Shivanand Bhatt, Advocate, with Mr. A.M.Saklani, Advocate, learned counsel for the
petitioners.
Mr. I.P.Kohli, learned Standing Counsel, for the respondent no1- State of Uttarakhand.
Date December 20, 2012.
Hon'ble B.S.Verma, J.(Oral)
(Interim Relief Application No. 13627 of 2012)
 By means of this writ petition, the petitioners have
sought the following relief:-
 "Issue an appropriate order or direction allowing the
application 6C2 of the petitioners filed before the court below
under Order 39 Rule 1&2 C.P.C. read with Section 151 C.P.C. and
further restrain the respondents from constructing the said water
tank over the land in question till the pendency of O.S. No. 60/2012
before the court below."
 Heard learned counsel for the petitioners.
 It appears from a perusal of the record that petitioners
Desh Raj and others filed a suit against the respondents, which was
registered as O.S. No. 60 of 2012 in the Court of Civil Judge
(Senior Division) Roorkee, district Haridwar. The trial Court on
the application (paper no. 6C2) moved by the plaintiff-petitioners
for temporary injunction passed an order dated 30-5-2012 for issue
of notices to the defendants fixing 6-7-2012 for objection and
disposal of the application under Order 39, Rule 1 & 2 read with
Section 151 C.P.C.
 In this writ petition, the petitioners have not assailed
the order dated 30-5-2012 passed by the trial Court. The date fixed
before the trial Court was 6-7-2012. Till now, the opposite parties-defendants might have appeared before the trial Court, therefore,

2
the Court cannot issue an injunction order without hearing to the
defendant-respondents.
 In the above facts and circumstances, the writ petition
being devoid of merit is liable to be dismissed outright at the
threshold.
 The writ petition is dismissed summarily. However, it
is directed that the trial Court shall hear and dispose of the
application for temporary injunction in accordance with law, moved
by the plaintiff-petitioners on its own merits, after hearing both the
parties, expeditiously within a period of three months as far as
possible from the date of production of a certified copy of this
order. If the defendant-respondents have not been served, the
petitioners shall be at liberty to serve them Dasti and the trial Court
is also directed to allow the plaintiffs to serve "Dasti" upon the
private defendant-respondents.
